provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: antecedent witness is the Mame, Tours 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam); 85% of the 1962 body's tokens align in order after canon folding; the witness text layer damages 'Lucize' where the 1962 prints 'Luciae'; the witness text layer damages 'pis devotidnis' where the 1962 prints 'piae devotionis'; the Mame prints j where the 1962 prints i (Iesum/Jesum, eius/ejus) and its recogniser renders the ae ligature as 'z' or 'e'; both are orthographic; pointing: the antecedent's reading is recorded verbatim above so its commas and colons can be compared, but its punctuation is NOT safely collatable - the recogniser turns commas into full stops, semicolons and question marks - so no punctuation difference here should be read as a difference between the printings; the 1962 prints the conclusion as 'Per Dominum.'; conclusion length was excluded from the alignment and is recorded here as printed, per the settled rule. Corroboration: Pustet 1862 text-layer lines 99438-99449 (65% coverage); Benziger 1962 conformed printing at line 84808 (75%; comparison only, never a publication basis). Recorded limitation: The antecedent reading is taken from that witness's text layer, not from a page image, so its letterforms are inferred rather than read; only the 1962 target was read on a page. I did not collate the antecedent's Introit, readings, chants or any Secunda Oratio / Alia Secreta / Alia Postcommunio.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Accepta tibi sit, Domine, sacratae plebis oblatio pro tuorum honore
Sanctorum: quorum se meritis de tribulatione percepisse cognoscit auxilium.
Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
